facts.statement: The genus Gallornis was described by Lambrecht in 1931.
Gallornis straeleni lived approximately 140 to 130 million years ago near Auxerre in the Yonne department of France.
facts.quote: The single known species Gallornis straeleni lived near today's Auxerre in Yonne département (France); it has been dated very tentatively to the Berriasian-Hauterivian stages, that is about 140–130 million years ago.

facts.statement: Researchers propose that Gallornis fossils display features found only in Neornithes, the group of birds living today.
facts.quote: It has been proposed that the remains show features only known from the Neornithes – the group of birds that exists today.

facts.statement: Gallornis fossils suggest that ancestors of all living birds were an evolutionary lineage distinct from Hesperornithes and Ichthyornithes as early as 130 million years ago.
facts.quote: Thus, the Gallornis fossils suggest that as early as about 130 million years ago or more the ancestors of all living birds might already have been an evolutionary lineage distinct from the closely related Hesperornithes and Ichthyornithes

facts.statement: During the time of Gallornis, its habitat was located around 30°N, north of the Tropic of Cancer aridity belt.
facts.quote: During the time of Gallornis, its range was located around 30°N, north of the Tropic of Cancer aridity belt.

facts.statement: Given the hot and humid Cretaceous climate, the habitat of Gallornis likely resembled West Africa around the Gulf of Guinea.
facts.quote: However, the Cretaceous was a hot and humid age in general, so the habitat might have more resembled West Africa around the Gulf of Guinea.

facts.statement: Gallornis lived alongside many non-avian dinosaurs around the Second Tethys Sea.
facts.quote: Gallornis was a contemporary of many (non-avian) dinosaurs living around the (Second) Tethys Sea.

facts.statement: Gallornis was allied with the Paleocene Scaniornis to form the supposed family Scaniornithidae or Torotigidae, a hypothesis that may be incorrect.
facts.quote: It was allied with the Paleocene Scaniornis, a probable waterbird that is sometimes allied with flamingos (which may or may not be correct and altogether is not too unlikely) to form the supposed "proto-flamingo" family Scaniornithidae or "Torotigidae" sensu Brodkorb.

facts.statement: A more probable hypothesis is that Gallornis was an early member of the Galloanserae clade, which includes modern landfowl and waterfowl.
facts.quote: A more probable hypothesis, echoing the initial description of 1931, is that Gallornis was an early member of the Galloanserae, the clade that eventually brought forth the Galliformes (landfowl) and Anseriformes (waterfowl) of our time.

facts.statement: Hartman et al. (2019) noted that Gallornis is too fragmentary to be confidently referred to Maniraptoromorpha, leading to its exclusion from phylogenetic analysis.
facts.quote: However, Hartman et al. (2019) noted in their supplementary material that Gallornis is too fragmentary for a confident referral within Maniraptoromorpha along with other fragmentary taxa (Valdoraptor, Unquillosaurus, Canadaga), which lead to their exclusion from phylogenetic analysis.

facts.statement: The Paleobi Database lists the parent group of Gallornis as Torotigidae.
The Paleobi Database lists the family of Gallornis as Torotigidae.
The Paleobi Database records the time range of Gallornis as the Hauterivian stage, from 132.6 to 125.77 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Hauterivian to Hauterivian (132.6 to 125.77 million years ago)

rejected.statement: The only known fossils of Gallornis are a worn partial femur and a fragment of a humerus.
rejected.quote: The known fossil material consists of a worn partial femur and a fragment of the humerus.
